newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco bonds rise on news of settlement progress.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco bonds rise on news of settlement progress.

text.p: Spreads on bonds from tobacco companies tightened significantly on Thursday on news that the states and the tobacco industry were close to reaching a liability settlement, traders and analysts said.
Spreads on RJR Nabisco debt tightened 10-25 basis points while spreads on Philip Morris Cos Inc debt tightened five to eight basis points, traders said.

Lisa Gaffney, a debt analyst who follows tobacco at Bear Stearns & Co Inc, said spreads on tobacco company bonds were now approaching the tigher end of their trading range since settlement talks had begun.
Gaffney believed there was room for the bonds to tighten further if the terms of the settlement were considered favorable to the tobacco industry.
"The degree of tightening will be affected as people put pen to paper and see what the financial impact will be," she said.
She noted important considerations for bond investors would the size of the settlement and how the issue of future liabilites was resolved.
Gaffney added investors would also be closely watching the reaction of rating agencies to any potential settlement.
Of particular interest is whether RJR Nabisco debt would be able to preserve its investment-grade rating if a settlement is reached, said Gaffney.
RJR Nabisco debt is currently rated only one notch above junk bond status at Baa3/BBB-minus. Philip Morris debt is perched more comfortably in investment-grade territory at A2/A.
Standard & Poor's currently has both Philip Morris and RJR Nabisco debt on CreditWatch negative. Moody's Investors Service has not watch-listed either company's debt rating.
